ia.name: Research proposal
ia.limit: 2,200 words (SL and HL; weighted 30% at SL, 20% at HL)

criteria.name: Introduction
look: A focused research question about a clearly identified population of interest
Relevant psychological theory and research explained, not just named
A clear rationale for why the question is worth investigating
Key terms and variables or phenomena defined

criteria.name: Research methodology
look: One of the class-practical methods (experiment, observation, survey/questionnaire or interview) chosen and justified for this question
Sampling technique and participants described and justified for the population
Procedure described in enough detail to be followed
Ethical considerations specific to the proposal addressed

criteria.name: Data collection
look: A data-collection tool (at least five items) designed for the research question and included in the appendix
Each item or measure clearly linked to what it is meant to capture
How the data would be recorded and analysed explained
Issues of measurement (reliability, validity, credibility) considered

criteria.name: Discussion
look: Strengths and limitations of the proposed design discussed with reference to the concepts (e.g. bias, measurement)
Likely sources of bias identified, with how they would be reduced
How far the findings could be generalized or transferred considered
Realistic modifications or follow-up research suggested

checklist: The research question names the population and what you will investigate
Background research is cited and actually explained in relation to your question
Your chosen method matches one of the class practical methods and you justify it over the alternatives
Sampling technique and sample size are stated and suit the population of interest
Ethics are specific: consent (including parental consent for minors), withdrawal, confidentiality, debriefing
The data-collection tool has at least five items and is in the appendix
You explain how the data would be analysed (e.g. descriptive statistics or thematic analysis)
Bias and measurement issues are discussed for YOUR design, not in generic terms
The proposal is within 2,200 words; references and appendices are excluded

examTips: Describe studies precisely: researcher(s) and year, aim, procedure, results, and the conclusion linked to the question asked.
In unseen scenarios, apply theory to the details given in the text rather than writing a generic essay.
Use the named concepts explicitly: say how bias, measurement or causality affects what a study can claim.
Correlation is not causation: only a true experiment with controlled variables supports a causal claim.
When evaluating, give a reason for every strength or limitation (why it matters for validity, credibility or generalization).
